newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Ruling coalition leader President Chandrika Kumaratunga and opposition leader Ranil Wickremesinghe appeal for calm at today's elections, where Sri Lankans vote to elect local government councils.
Defence officials ask whether the Sri Lanka Air Force helicopter gunship that went missing over the northeast on Wednesday was sabotaged.
President Kumaratunga appeals to supporters of all political parties not to be provoked into committing acts of violence on polling day.
Police take into custody a worker at a printing press in Kandy in central Sri Lanka, together with a stock of forged ballot papers.
President Kumaratunga launches a private sector sponsored programme to train youth for employment.
Nearly 10 million Sri Lankan voters go to the polls today to elect councillors to 238 local bodies.

Contrary to reports there are no Russian passport holders engaged in Sri Lanka's battle against Tamil rebels, says a senior Russian Federation diplomat. Some reports said there were Russian pilots in the helicopter gunship which went missing on Wednesday.
